engine: crownd/finest's editorial pair — a portrait RENDER in a fixed clipping FRAME on one side + a serif HEADING/body on the other. As the section passes through the viewport the image SCALES UP within its frame (a scroll-scrubbed Ken-Burns BOUND to the frame: the frame clips, the image grows ~1.0 -> ~1.14) while the copy holds; the copy rises in once on enter. Harvested from D_finest (F3: 'Architektur vom Allerfeinsten' render + copy, render zooms on scroll).

measured_teardown.move: two scroll-triggers on the section. (1) a SCRUB over the section's whole pass through the viewport (start 'top bottom', end 'bottom top'): the image transform scale = zoomFrom + p*(zoomTo-zoomFrom) (default 1.0 -> 1.14), optional translateY drift for parallax. The frame is overflow:hidden so the zoom is clipped to the frame, not a full-bleed grow. (2) a one-shot REVEAL of the copy ([data-zoomcopy]) on enter at 'top 72%': opacity 0->1 + translateY 26px->0, ~0.9s cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1). L/R sides swap via .szp--rtl. set(p) is a PURE scrub of the zoom.
measured_teardown.cited: finest: a portrait render (left) + 'Architektur vom Allerfeinsten' serif heading + body (right); on scroll the render gently scales/parallax-zooms within its frame while the copy holds.

zoomFrom.what: image scale when the section enters (bottom of viewport).

zoomTo.what: image scale when it leaves (top of viewport). The frame clips the overflow.

drift.what: optional vertical parallax of the image across the pass (+/- drift); 0 = pure zoom.

ease.what: scrub ease (linear so the zoom tracks scroll 1:1; the copy reveal has its own cubic-bezier).

revealCopy.what: reveal the copy once on enter (opacity + rise); false = copy always shown.

start.what: ScrollTrigger start for the zoom scrub (section top hits viewport bottom).

end.what: ScrollTrigger end for the zoom scrub (section bottom hits viewport top).

manageLenis.what: own a Lenis instance if present; false when the page drives a shared Lenis (lab sets false).

entry: ScrollZoomImagePair.create(target, opts) -> { trigger, reveal, lenis, set(p), refresh(), destroy }. target = .szp-stage > .szp-figure(.szp-frame > img) + .szp-copy([data-zoomcopy]). Add .szp--rtl to swap sides. set(p 0..1) is a PURE scrub of the zoom.
law: transform scale + translateY (the image) + opacity/translateY (copy reveal) + overflow clip (the frame) only; GPU; NO mix-blend / NO backdrop; NO WebGL; reduced-motion or <=820px -> static (image at zoomFrom, copy shown). owns_pin false (the section is NOT pinned — the zoom scrubs across its natural pass through the viewport). GSAP + ScrollTrigger required; set(p) standalone.
gate_mode: scroll-scrub (not pinned). Verify: the image scale ramps zoomFrom -> zoomTo across the section's pass; the FRAME clips it (overflow hidden — the image grows but the frame box doesn't); the copy reveals once on enter; .szp--rtl swaps sides. Distinct from a full-bleed hero Ken-Burns (that's not framed/clipped or paired with held copy). Smoothness via the scroll path.
proven: lab: two L/R pairs on OUR QUADRO renders (day-front + a serif heading, then terrace rtl). Measured live: zoom scale 1.0 -> 1.035 -> 1.07 -> 1.105 -> 1.14 across p (linear); frame overflow = hidden (clip confirmed); copy opacity -> 1 on enter. Screenshot (mid-zoom 1.07): the QUADRO render scaled within its 4:5 frame + 'Архітектура найвищого ґатунку' serif heading + body held beside (matches finest F2). Probe (4x CPU throttle, scroll-scrub): 1/618 long frames (0.2%), 59.9fps -> PASS. Zero console errors. Serif stand-in = Playfair Display (Canela / PP-Editorial class).
